generation.prompt:
Draw a NEW kinetic 2D fighting-game animation study of SHARK, using the attached image ONLY for character identity and costume. The current character drawings feel stiff; this sheet must solve that through BODY MECHANICS, not extra effects.

This is the selected "LOW SCOOP" two-hit rising-hook attack. Keep compact shoulder-led fencing swagger as his personality, but make the action feel like a moving athlete: deeply compressed knees, asymmetric weight-bearing, hips leading the torso, ribcage twisting against pelvis, one shoulder genuinely advancing, a changing spine curve, planted foot pushing through the ground, the other heel lifting and pivoting. Alternate compression and extension. Never repeat the same upright torso across frames. Each drawing is a passing moment in one continuous swing, NOT a catalogue of evenly balanced character poses. Hands, elbows, shoulders and hips lead/follow naturally. Hair, sash and ropes lag a beat behind the body; never turn into a huge plume. Controlled athletic exaggeration, no rubber limbs or broken joints.

Make a clean 1536x1024 animator's key-pose sheet, 3 columns by 2 rows, 6 generous full-body panels on warm off-white. Thin subtle panel dividers, small labels 01 COIL / 02 LOAD / 03 SCOOP / 04 RISE / 05 RELEASE / 06 RESET. All poses face RIGHT, consistent side-on game camera and anatomy scale, whole body and complete weapon visible; same head size across poses. Clear black pencil/ink contours and flat teal/slate/brown cel shading with small ivory highlights. More alive and gestural than a polished character turnaround. No hitboxes, no logo. NO motion blur, no smear frames, no duplicated limbs, NO big energy effects; the body and weapon positions alone must sell the movement. Tiny weapon path arrows are allowed but should not obscure silhouette.

CHARACTER LOCK: athletic muscular adult man with long swept-back low-volume white hair, blue sports wraparound glasses, sleeveless teal scale armor, one small bone shoulder guard, brown chest straps, rope belt, loose slate trousers, brown strapped boots, teal waist sash. Two arms, two legs. Anatomical RIGHT hand ALWAYS holds one long wood shaft with one silver SINGLE C hook, never a sword or trident. Anatomical LEFT hand ALWAYS holds the short triangular knife, carried safely rearward for counterbalance. Hook shaft stays constant length across all frames. No face paint. Keep face, clothing and silhouette recognizably identical to attached Shark.

Choreography in reading order:
01 COIL: leaving the shoulder-rest idle, hook comes down from the right shoulder, rear heel starts to lift, chest rotates BACK against front-facing hips, right elbow folds, front knee begins bending. Head and gaze remain on opponent to the right. An inclined S-shaped spine, not upright mannequin.
02 LOAD: deepest asymmetric compression. Weight sinks over bent rear hip then drives toward bent front knee; back boot pushes from ball of foot, shoulders low and twisted. Right hand takes hook down in front near ankle height, left knife arm stretches naturally backward for counterbalance. Head lower than first pose, muscles compressed; purposeful crouch, not a static squat.
03 SCOOP: first hit. Hips drive forward FIRST, rear heel lifts decisively, torso unwinds, right shoulder and elbow whip forward in a rising scoop with hook now in front at abdomen-to-chest height. Front knee still deeply bent. Chest leaning diagonally forward, left knife trails behind. This is explosive movement with weight transfer, NOT the previous pose with only an arm repositioned.
04 RISE: second hit. Push powerfully through front boot into a long diagonally rising body line; pelvis rotates, chest opens, head tracks hook upward-right, right arm extends through an overhead/front hook position. Rear leg extends back and heel is off ground. Shoulder visibly raised and torso stretched compared with03. Whole chain ankle-knee-hip-ribcage-shoulder-elbow follows one rising C curve. Hook arc stays in FRONT and above the opponent, not a somersault.
05 RELEASE: a real overshoot and braking pose. Right arm eases past the high strike, elbow softens; shoulders roll forward, front knee bends again absorbing momentum, back foot catches weight. Head dips slightly as hair and sash still trail from the rise. Hook starts falling toward the shoulder-rest path. Do not freeze rigidly overhead.
06 RESET: relaxed asymmetrical recovery, weight settles back, right hook shaft approaching the shoulder, torso unwinds toward his familiar swagger. Knife hand drops naturally. NOT identical to01; show the last residual turn and delayed sash motion.

Prioritize convincing shifting weight, strong lines of action, clear timing extremes, loose shoulders and an unbroken low-to-high weapon path. Keep the natural asymmetry in every single pose.
